title: RedHen Labs automation rule
description: Shape of an automation in RedHen Labs. Conditions are evaluated over a lookback window; entities satisfying ALL conditions receive the action. Actions are proposals unless auto_apply is true. The rule engine as a whole is on the Professional plan, so every automation described here needs it.

type.description: Which automation this is. NOT a wire field: the API ignores it, because the type is decided by the endpoint you post to (/api/automations, /api/automations/harvest, /api/automations/negative, /api/automations/dayparting, and so on). It is here so a reader can tell which of the fields below apply.

campaign_ids.description: Amazon campaign IDs this automation may touch — IDs, never campaign names. Required on every type except harvest, which scopes itself with source_campaign_ids and destination_campaign_match_types instead. A campaign may carry only one bid automation, one negative automation and one dayparting schedule.

schedule_interval.description: How often the automation runs. Anything outside this list is rejected. Budget automations additionally accept "2_hours". Dayparting ignores this entirely — it reconciles continuously.

auto_apply.description: false = propose and wait for your approval. true = act unattended. Off until you switch it on, one automation at a time.

status.description: A paused automation is left in place and stops running. Dayparting accepts it when the automation is created; the other types are paused and resumed afterwards.

rules.description: Evaluated in array order, and that order IS the precedence: where two rules would change the same field, the earlier one wins.

name.description: For your own reading. The bid endpoint replaces it with the rule's position ("Rule 1", "Rule 2", ...).

lookback_days.description: Metrics are SUMMED over this window, not averaged. A longer window makes any threshold easier to trip. Hard capped at 90 days: a bid automation is rejected above that, and the harvest and negative engines clamp to it at run time.

conditions.description: ALL conditions must hold (logical AND). A metric the target has no data for fails the condition rather than guessing.

metric.description: "cvr" is the conversion rate; there is no "conversion_rate". "conversions" is an alias for orders, and the bid-automation editor does not offer it. "bid" is the target's current effective bid.

actions.description: The action verb is the KEY — there is no separate type/mode/value. Percent or dollars is chosen by the key itself (_pct vs _dollar). One verb per rule: the engine works through the verbs in its own fixed order and acts on the first one present, so a second verb in the same rule is ignored rather than combined. The remaining keys are settings, not verbs.

increase_bid_pct.description: Raise the bid by this percentage.

increase_bid_dollar.description: Raise the bid by this many dollars.

decrease_bid_pct.description: Lower the bid by this percentage.

decrease_bid_dollar.description: Lower the bid by this many dollars.

set_bid_dollar.description: Set the bid to this exact amount. The only action that is not bounded by min_bid or max_bid — the amount you name IS the bid.

set_bid_to_cpc.description: Set the bid to the target's measured CPC. Skipped, with a reason, if the target has no clicks and therefore no CPC.

cpc_times_acos_ratio.description: Set the bid to CPC x (target_acos / actual ACoS). Set target_acos beside it; with none set the engine aims at 30. Skipped if either CPC or actual ACoS is unmeasured.

bid_times_acos_ratio.description: Set the bid to the current bid x (target_acos / actual ACoS). Set target_acos beside it; with none set the engine aims at 30. Skipped if actual ACoS is unmeasured.

pause_targeting.description: Pause the keyword or product target.

add_negative.description: Negative automations. Add the search term as a negative.

target_acos.description: Setting, not a verb. The ACoS the two ratio actions aim at. Defaults to 30 if omitted.

min_bid.description: Setting, not a verb. Floor for this rule, and it binds in both directions: a floor also pulls a bid UP to reach it. Omitted, increase_bid_pct and increase_bid_dollar run with no floor at all, and every other bounded action falls back to $0.10 — so set it explicitly if you care where the bottom is.

max_bid.description: Setting, not a verb. Ceiling for this rule, applied PER RULE from inside its own actions — there is no automation-level max_bid. THE PRIMARY SAFETY PROPERTY: set it on every rule that raises a bid. Omitted, the engine falls back to $10.00.

match_type.description: Negative automations. The single match type to negate at.

match_types.description: Negative automations only, where it creates one negative per match type listed and is read in preference to match_type. With both absent the engine uses exact. A bid automation does not keep this key.

negative_level.description: A preference, honoured where it changes the outcome. Campaign level applies only to Sponsored Products campaigns with more than one enabled ad group. Sponsored Brands has no campaign-level negative keyword, and a negative PRODUCT target (an ASIN) is ad-group only on Amazon — both are placed at the ad group whatever this says. In a single-ad-group campaign the two levels block identical traffic, so the ad group is used.

action.description: NOT A FIELD. The engine reads `actions`, plural, keyed by the action verb. A rule posted with `action` is accepted and stored with an empty actions object: it matches targets and then changes nothing, with no error anywhere. This key must not be present.

reason.description: Free-text commentary for a human reader. Nothing in the engine reads it.

source_campaign_ids.description: Harvest only. Amazon campaign IDs to harvest search terms OUT of — IDs, never campaign names.

destination_campaign_match_types.description: Harvest only. Maps each destination campaign ID to the match types to create there, e.g. {"123456789": ["exact", "phrase"]}. A destination may not also be a source, and may not be an AUTO campaign — AUTO campaigns accept neither keywords nor product targets.

default_bid.description: Harvest only. Starting bid for each keyword created in the destination.

add_negative_to_source.description: Harvest only. Add the harvested term as a negative exact in the source campaign. A deliberate choice, not a rule — see docs/negative-keywords.md. The engine will not negate into a campaign that is also a destination.

timezone.description: Dayparting only. The seller's zone, as an IANA name so daylight saving is handled rather than assumed.

lead_minutes.description: Dayparting only. Both edges of every window are shifted EARLIER by this much, because Amazon propagates a bid change with a delay and writing at the exact boundary loses the edge of the window every day.

windows.description: Dayparting only. Reconciled continuously, not fired as a schedule; the original bid is restored when a window closes. One window covers ONE day, so a Monday-to-Friday schedule is five windows. Windows may not overlap — two adjustments covering the same minute would fight each other every hour.

end.description: HH:MM, 24-hour. May be earlier than start, which means the window crosses midnight. It may not equal start.

percent.description: Percent-only; there is no absolute adjustment. An increase is capped at 100 — a window can at most double the bid you set yourself — and a decrease at 99, because 100 is not a bid, it is a pause. Every adjustment is computed from your baseline bid, never from the live bid, so adjustments cannot compound.

explanation.description: Human/LLM-readable statement of the decision this rule encodes. Documentation only; the API ignores it.

notes.description: Documentation only; the API ignores it.
